title: LTS channel service safeguards and automated unwind plan
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a cross-surface plan that combines: deterministic LTS channel guarantees, per-surface service-level safeguards, and an automated unwind (rollback / degrade) playbook. The goal is a runnable set of configs, checks, and tooling so a single binary/manifest change that causes outages or regressions can be automatically contained and reverted without manual choreography across runtime, API, SDKs, and console.
background: We currently have ad-hoc rollback procedures for hosted runtime incidents and separate manual rollbacks for console/API SDK releases. As Dedicated and Private customers grow, we need an interoperable LTS safety surface: an automated containment flow that spans model/runtime binaries, API schema changes, SDK minor bumps, and console feature toggles. Existing artifacts (compat matrices and channel policies) are fragmented; this ticket produces the executable plan and the small set of components required to operate it.
goals: 1) Define per-surface safeguards and a minimal compatibility contract for LTS lines. 2) Implement an automated unwind orchestration that can: detect regression signals, restrict traffic to stable variants, and run staged rollback across surfaces. 3) Add observability and canary gates so rollouts abort automatically on SLO regressions. 4) Document runbook and provide emergency CLI for on-call.
scope: Included: runtime binary pinning rules, API schema backward-compat checks, SDK runtime compatibility checks, console rollout flags, canary metric thresholds, automation runbook, and CI/CD pipeline hooks. Excluded: full model-versioning/backwards-incompatible model releases and long-term policy governance (will be a follow-up).
out_of_scope: Deep changes to customer-facing SDK major versioning policy; dedicated contract negotiation for enterprise customers (handled via Account Engineering).
proposed_design:
- LTS compatibility contract: each LTS line published with a compatibility manifest (human-readable and machine-parseable) listing supported runtime ABI, API schema version, min SDK patch, console flags.
- Safeguards per surface: runtime offers a 'safety-mode' binary which can be toggled to enable conservative scheduling & fallback; API surface exposes a feature-compat endpoint that returns compatible SDK/API pairs; SDKs read a remote compatibility manifest and refuse risky automatic upgrades when pinned.
- Automated unwind: a controller (k8s controller for hosted/dedicated) that subscribes to observability signals (latency/error rate tokenized metrics). When threshold breached, the controller: (a) reduces traffic cohort percentage to stable channel, (b) flips console feature flags to safe variants, (c) orchestrates rollback of incompatible SDK deployments in browser clients via prompting and telemetry, and (d) opens a high-priority incident with pre-populated context.
- Rollout gates: metric-based (p50/p95 latency, error rate, end-to-end success ratio), cohort size limit, time-window checks, and external dependency health (e.g., model store).
compatibility_summary: We will maintain a compact compatibility matrix (represented as the compatibility manifest) with entries like: runtime:1.22.x <-> API:v3.1 <-> SDK-min:2.4.5 <-> console-flag:stable. Key design is machine-readable manifests and a small stable surface of checks that CI can validate during release. The manifest is intentionally conservative: SDKs will accept runtime >= min and <= max patch ranges, but not semantic-breaking minor bumps without explicit opt-in.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Conservative manifests reduce fast-path upgrades for customers but increase safety.
- Automating rollback across surfaces is complex and may produce transient inconsistency (e.g., console showing controls not matching client SDK). We'll mitigate via staged cohorting and explicit UI degradation modes.
- Reliance on observability signals means false positives could trigger unnecessary unwinds; threshold tuning and a short human-in-the-loop window (1 minute configurable) is included.
rollout_gates: 1) Canary cohort (1% of traffic) for 24h with p95 < baseline + 20% and error rate < baseline + 2% absolute. 2) Expanded cohorts (10%, 50%) after automated health checks pass. 3) Block expand if external model-store or infra region has degraded. 4) Final expansion requires release manager ACK or automatic pass after 72h.
upgrade_tooling_changes:
- CI step: validate compatibility manifest and run cross-surface dry-run asserting SDK/API/runtime pairings.
- Add 'unwind-controller' as a deployable microservice with RBAC and audit logs.
- SDK: lightweight manifest consumer library and opt-in auto-upgrade policy.
- Console: show live compatibility status per account and allow emergency toggle for safety-mode.
- Release pipeline: add post-deploy gating job that writes deployment fingerprint to manifest registry and monitors the canary metrics for 60-90 minutes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Compatibility manifest format agreed and spec PR merged.
- Unwind-controller prototype can detect a synthetic regression and execute a three-step containment in staging (traffic redirection, flag flip, rollback marker).
- CI includes manifest validation; a simulated incompatibility blocks the merge.
- Runbook documented and onboarded with 2 SREs and 2 runtime engineers.
- End-to-end test added to release pipeline that exercises canary gating logic.
